intro: Lesson 37. Read each word slowly, pointing with your finger. Only the Arabic is the Qur'an; the English is a translation of its meaning.

arabic.text: وَتَكُونُ ٱلْجِبَالُ كَٱلْعِهْنِ ٱلْمَنفُوشِ (٥) فَأَمَّا مَن ثَقُلَتْ مَوَٰزِينُهُۥ (٦) فَهُوَ فِى عِيشَةٍۢ رَّاضِيَةٍۢ (٧) وَأَمَّا مَنْ خَفَّتْ مَوَٰزِينُهُۥ (٨)

head: Ayah
Translation of the meaning (Saheeh International)
rows: And the mountains will be like wool, fluffed up.
Then as for one whose scales are heavy [with good deeds],
He will be in a pleasant life.
But as for one whose scales are light,

questions.q: Chunk and link Al-Qari'ah 101:5-8 with the teacher.
Listening turns: today's group says 101:5-8 to the teacher, one by one. Everyone else: say it softly 3 times looking, 3 times without.
questions.a: Pupil recites with no help; the teacher marks hifdh and tajweed on the rubric and gives one target.

questions.q: Name two good deeds that make the scales heavy.

questions.a: A) Those with many good deeds. 101:6 to 7: heavy scales: a pleasant life.

questions.q: Al-Qari'ah 101:6: «فَأَمَّا مَن ...» Which word comes next?
Think again: The mountains will be like fluffy wool (101:5)! What is the heaviest thing you can think of, and what makes our good-deed scales heavy?
questions.a: Mountains are very heavy, yet they become like wool. Good deeds make our scales heavy (101:6).
